chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Jamil, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"Fine flour (for bread) for wheat, and sique (coarse flour) for fine flour, equal for equal, there is no objection to it."

key_terms.الدَّقِيقُ: Fine flour, typically used for bread
key_terms.السَّوِيقُ: Coarse flour or semolina, often used for specific dishes
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection to it / it is permissible
key_terms.مِثْلًا بِمِثْلٍ: Equal for equal, a key condition in commodity exchange to avoid usury

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exchanging different types of flour in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that exchanging different grades of the same commodity (like wheat for fine flour) is permissible under the *mithlan bi-mithl* (equal for equal) rule, provided the exchange is immediate and equal in measure. It addresses the specific juristic nuance of whether varying quality levels constitute a hidden excess (*riba al-fadl*) or merely a fair trade of distinct units, affirming its validity in Shia fiqh. This ruling facilitates commercial flexibility while maintaining the core prohibition of usury in spot transactions.
